metadata.title: input-output-hk/rnd-midgard (Lean blueprint)

extraction_notes.note: 24 environments have an empty body (only a title and a Lean \label); their statement is the verbatim \begin...\end text without the label, so the finishing step cannot match them to their environment facts.
Hard rule 6 (every labelled result is a node) vs core rule 1 (verbatim statement) for empty environments: kept the nodes with the bare environment text rather than dropping them.
definition or theorem: Induction Step Machine is a definition environment whose body asserts an induction principle; typed theorem, and its empty companion likewise.
\ref{dfn:Tests.ordered_list_tests} does not resolve (the label is thm:Tests.ordered_list_tests); the edge from the test battery was added by hand.
The three reachable-list theorems share the identical text 'The registered list is a valid (reachable) state.' (copy-paste in source); kept as three nodes by their titles.
Figures, the Issues list of GitHub issues, \martin/\redflag author comments and module descriptions of the Lean files were not extracted as nodes.

metadata.extraction_comment: This is a Lean formalization blueprint: most theorems are proved only in Lean and have no proof in the text, and dependencies between them are inferred from shared definitions.

nodes.name: Computational Relation
nodes.statement: A relation \(\mathcal{R} \subseteq E \times A \times S \times S \) is computational if and only if there is a function \(f : E \times A \times S \to S_{\mathsf{Errors}}\) such that \[ \forall (e \in E) (a \in A) (s_{i}, s_{o} \in S), (e, a, s_{i}, s_{o}) \in \mathcal{R} \iff f(e,a,s_{i}) = \eta(s_{o}) \]
nodes.statement_short: A relation is computational iff some function returns exactly the related output state (wrapped) for every environment, action and input state.
nodes.label: dfn:computational_relation

nodes.name: From Initial State
nodes.statement: Given a State Machine \(\mathsf{sm}\), we say that a state \(s\) is reach from the initial state \(\mathsf{sm.init}\) if there are 0 or more \(\mathsf{sm}\)-steps from \(\mathsf{sm.init}\) to \(s\).
nodes.label: dfn:ComputationalRelation.StateMachine.FromInit

nodes.name: After Initial State
nodes.statement: Given a State Machine \(\mathsf{sm}\), we say that a state \(s\) is reach from the initial state \(\mathsf{sm.init}\) if there are 1 or more \(\mathsf{sm}\)-steps from \(\mathsf{sm.init}\) to \(s\).
nodes.label: dfn:ComputationalRelation.StateMachine.AfterInit

nodes.name: Induction Step Machine
nodes.statement: Given a predicate that is valid for the initial state and as an invariant over the relation steps, we can prove the predicate holds for all reachable states.

Transaction Information
nodes.statement: {Transaction Information} Transaction are a tuple providing: \begin{description} \item[validity internal] execution time bounds. When missing, they are assumed to by minus infinity and plus infinity. \item[value] the amount of value in the transaction \item[fee] the fee of the transaction \item[validator] who is signing the transaction \item[transaction id] \end{description}

nodes.name: Tokens
nodes.statement: Tokens are structures containing a name, (polymorphic) data and id. Tokens are records with: \begin{description} \item[id] same as its reference \item[data] keeping internal data \item[name] the name of the token \end{description}

nodes.statement: The element position in the list is its id, and thus, all elements have a unique id since we only append elements.

assumptions: The element position in the list is its id
conclusions: all elements have a unique id

nodes.statement: When minting, we just append a new value, and when burning, we just mark it as no element.
nodes.name: Minting and burning tokens

nodes.statement: The key-unordered list data structure \emph{assumes} keys are unique, while the key-ordered list data structure inserts them in strict order guaranteeing they are unique and sorted.
nodes.name: Key-unordered and key-ordered lists

nodes.statement: Each element in the key-ordered list represents the element and a range of elements that are not in the list.
nodes.name: Key-ordered list element range

nodes.statement: To add elements in either of these lists, we need to mint a token with the information we want to add, and to remove an element, we simply burn such token.
nodes.name: Adding and removing list elements

nodes.statement: To prove that an element is in the list, we just show a token that contains its as the mere existence of the token shows membership plus the correct \emph{Spending/Minting Policies}.
nodes.name: Membership proof

nodes.statement: To prove that an element is not in the list, we need to show the element is not where it should be, this requires the list to be sorted.
nodes.name: Non-membership proof
List Element
nodes.statement: List nodes are records with: \begin{description} \item[key] (optional) indicates the current node key, \item[link] (optional) indicates the next key in the list, \item[data] polymorphic element depending on the use of the list. \end{description}

nodes.statement: We define operators directory as three lists: one unordered for registered operators, and two ordered for active and retired operators.

nodes.name: State Transitions
nodes.statement: Operators can perform the following actions: \begin{description} \item[Activate] activates registered operators \item[Retire] retires active operators \item[Register] registers an operator by placing a bond, the operator is the one forging the transaction. \item[Deregister] deregisters an operator (if possible) \item[RemoveDuplicateSlashBond] removes fraudulent operator \item[RecoverBond] returns (if possible) the bond to a retired operator \item[ActRemoveOperatorBad] removes a fraudulent active operators, used by BadSettlement and BadBlock \item[UpdateBondHold] updates bond holding time, used by New State and New Settlement \item[RetRemove] removes fraudulent retired operators, used by Bad State and Settlement. \end{description}
nodes.statement_short: Operator directory actions: activate, retire, register, deregister, slash duplicates, recover bond, remove bad active/retired, update bond hold.

nodes.statement: Finds if there are two elements in the registered queue with the same key and different times or there is an operator registered and active or registered and retired. Here we assume agents have a valid state of the onchain data structure.

nodes.name: OpsDir: find witness registered

nodes.statement: Assuming we can build a transaction \(\mathsf{tx}\) such that the time validity bounds in \(\mathsf{tx}\) fit inside the interval \([ \mathsf{sch.shift\_start} + \mathsf{shift\_duration} , \mathsf{sch.shift\_start} + 2*\mathsf{shift\_duration})\), then the next operator in line can claim control of the scheduler.

conclusions: the next operator in line can claim control of the scheduler
